Ambalika beholding the Rishi, became pale with fear And, O Bharata, beholding her so afflicted and pale with fear, Vyasa addressed her and said, 'Because thou hast been pale with fear at the sight of my grim visage, therefore, thy child shall be pale in complexion. O thou of handsome face, the name also thy child shall bear will be Pandu (the pale).'

issues.description: The invocation explicitly identifies Isana with Brahma, Vishnu and Hari. It does not explicitly link that referent to the true-light Brahma, Pitamaha Brahma emerging from the egg, or Brahma visiting Vyasa. Those references are retained separately pending evidence establishing identity; this does not assert that they are different beings.

The candidate's combined creation-and-visit Brahma entry has been separated because the batch does not explicitly establish that Pitamaha Brahma and the visiting Brahma are identical. Hiranyagarbha and Brahma Parameshthi are explicitly connected within the visit scene.
Parameshthi is explicitly named in the Prajapati list, so that mention is supported. Its identity with the visiting Brahma Parameshthi remains unresolved.

The supplied list prints Atma Vibhavasu without a separating comma. Whether this denotes one individual or separate individuals named Atma and Vibhavasu cannot be settled from this batch. The combined source label and its parent relationship are therefore provisional.

Mahya is called the youngest of these Vivaswans but is absent from the preceding enumeration of Div's sons. Div's parentage of Mahya and Mahya's sibling relationships to the enumerated sons depend on resolving that reference and remain provisional.
Sibling relationships are deductions from the listed common parentage, not explicit statements using a sibling term. Each symmetric pair is recorded once and marked provisional.

The all-pervading spirit is a singular reference in Vyasa's catalogue, but the passage does not establish whether it denotes an individual being or a philosophical principle. Its entity entry is provisional, with no identification to another entry.

The seven sons of Daksha, ten Prachetas, twin Aswins, children of Kuru and Pandu, other collective classes, and counted offspring of the three Jyotis are not individually distinguished in this batch. Counts and collective labels have not been converted into individual entities.
